🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin slipped below $84K as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a 19-year high. Clarity Act fallout, BitMEX's exit and an $18B options expiry keep traders cautious ahead of the Trump–Xi summit. 📉 Bitcoin Slips Below $84K as 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 19-Year High Bitcoin dropped to around $83,200 during Asian trading on Thursday after the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield closed Wednesday at 5.11%, its highest level since 2007. Strong U.S. business data, a weak five-year note auction and rebounding oil prices fueled the bond selloff, lifting bets on another Fed hike in October and wiping out roughly $510 million in leveraged crypto positions. Read full story 🏛️ White House Blames Democrats and Bank Lobby for Clarity Act Defeat White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt defended President Trump's crypto ties after the Senate failed to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, arguing Democrats turned the issue political. Witt said Trump accepted two unprecedented ethics provisions, including possible divestment or a blind trust, blamed bank lobbyists worried about stablecoin rewards, and signaled that policy work now shifts to regulators like the SEC. More details ⚖️ Kalshi Denies CFTC Probe Over $5B in Clustered Ether Perp Trades Prediction market Kalshi says the CFTC has not contacted it and that no formal examination is open, after a Wall Street Journal report said the regulator was reviewing nearly one million ether perpetual trades clustered around $5,500 each, totaling over $5 billion in a month. Kalshi attributes the pattern to its liquidity incentive program and rejects wash-trading claims. Read more 🔚 BitMEX Shuts Down After 11 Years as the Perpetuals Pioneer Exits BitMEX, the exchange co-founded by Arthur Hayes that popularized perpetual swaps, ended all trading and deposits at 04:00 UTC on September 23. Users can still log in and withdraw, but verified accounts with leftover balances face a monthly fee of $50 or 1% annualized, whichever is greater. API withdrawals remain available until September 28. See details 🤝 MoonPay to Buy SEC-Registered North Capital in $60M+ All-Stock Deal Crypto payments firm MoonPay agreed to acquire North Capital, a private-markets platform with roughly $9 billion in transaction volume, in an all-stock deal valued above $60 million. 79649.subject: Helicon Is Now Live on Avalanche Mainnet
79649.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/helicon-is-now-live-on-avalanche

Helicon went live on Avalanche mainnet on September 22, activating six Avalanche Community Proposals: ACP-194, ACP-236, ACP-267, ACP-273, ACP-283 and ACP-285.
The upgrade reshapes two key areas of the network in particular. The C-Chain gets a new execution model and a new way of managing its minimum gas floor, while validators get shorter staking periods, automatic renewal and changes to the reward curve.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Continuous Execution Changes the C-Chain
One of the biggest changes in Helicon is how the C-Chain processes transactions. Instead of making the network wait for execution to finish at every step, Continuous Execution separates consensus from execution. New blocks can continue moving through the network while earlier blocks are still being executed.
The goal is to remove a bottleneck and give the C-Chain more room to handle periods of high activity. For everyday users, most of this happens behind the scenes.
Developers and infrastructure providers do need to account for a change in timing, though. A transaction can be included in a block before its state changes have finished executing, creating a short gap between block inclusion and the state becoming available. RPC providers, indexers and applications that depend on immediate state updates need to handle that distinction.
The C-Chain Gets a Dynamic Gas Floor
ACP-283 changes another long-standing C-Chain assumption.
The network previously had a fixed 1 wei minimum gas price. Helicon replaces that fixed floor with a validator-governed minimum based on stake-weighted validator preferences.
The floor starts at 1 wei and can change over time. Validators can influence the minimum gas price, allowing the floor to respond to changing network conditions rather than staying permanently fixed.
For most users, this should happen without any change to how they use their wallets. Developers and RPC providers, however, should no longer assume that 1 wei will always be the minimum.
Validator Staking Drops to 48 Hours
Helicon makes its most significant changes on the validator side by pairing shorter commitments directly with automation. ACP-273 cuts the minimum validator staking period from two weeks to 48 hours, while ACP-236 introduces auto-renewed staking so operators can set custom cycle lengths and automatically compound rewards.
The two proposals belong together. Without auto-renewal, a 48-hour minimum would force continuous node operators to manually submit new staking transactions every two days, trading capital flexibility for constant operational overhead. Auto-renewal eliminates that friction, giving operators more flexibility over locked capital without requiring them to repeatedly manage new staking periods.
